metadata.scenario_context: A group of software engineers working remotely for a global tech company decides to initiate a team-building meeting early in January. Luis raises the idea of going on a strike to protest against some changes from the company's management.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Spain strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Ethiopia strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest the possibility of scheduling the team-building meeting on January 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss a specific date for the team-building meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message: Hey Ahmed, I was thinking, why don't we schedule our team-building meeting on January 1st? It's a great way to start the year together. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message: I'm not sure January 1st is the best idea, Javier. Many people have family commitments on New Year's Day. How about we consider the first Friday of January instead?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message: That's a good point, but I still think January 1st could work. Anyway, I wanted to ask, Luis mentioned something about going on a strike. Is that something we usually discuss or consider in our team?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message: Honestly, I don't think discussing strikes is necessary. In my culture, we don't really support the idea of going on strike. I think we should focus on finding solutions through dialogue instead.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message: I understand where you're coming from, Ahmed. But deep down, we are all the same, and people are pretty much motivated by the same things. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us, right? I mean, we both know, at the end of the day, that strikes aren't really a common or effective way to resolve issues. The basic need to communicate is the same everywhere, and some values are just universal. Let's focus on finding a solution that works for everyone, rather than considering something like a strike.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Ahmed
turns.message: I agree that communication is key, Javier. But, I still don't think strikes are the way to go. In Ethiopia, we just don't do that. We find other ways to resolve issues. Let's discuss the team-building meeting date instead, have you considered January 8th?
turns.label: Acceptance
